title: Pretraining batch 128 -> 96 records on the 081 Polar Express Muon incumbent (more optimizer steps, same wall-clock)
description: P02-context batch follow-up (no backlog P-idea; nearest P02 Muon): change only BS 128 -> 96 in 081-claude's pretrain.py, keeping every per-step hyperparameter, so the fixed 300 s buys more Muon updates (~5,300-5,700 vs 4,682-4,769) on fewer records (~3.2-3.5 vs 3.9 epochs). bs 256 -> 128 was a keep (+23, every seed) and bs 64 at the older WD-1x incumbent lost mainly through one collapsed seed (334/179/308 vs 319/293/335), so under today's 10x Muon weight decay and Polar Express updates the step-count optimum for handing expert iteration an adaptable model may lie between 64 and 128.
hypothesis: 066's bs-128 gain did not come from lower val loss and appeared in later EI rounds, pointing at the optimization path (more fixed-spectral-size Muon updates, more gradient noise, more cumulative decoupled decay) making a more RL-adaptable model. Val loss plateaus by ~75 s (step ~1000, <1 epoch) in 081, so records beyond ~1 epoch mainly feed memorization (train 0.06 vs val 0.095); trading ~13-18% of records for ~12-20% more updates should cost no fit. Timing model from 051/066/067: step time is GPU-bound at 128 (64 ms) but floors near ~50 ms at 64, so bs 96 should take ~53-57 ms/step. Cumulative Muon decay rises only ~15% (like MUON_WD ~11.5x, far from the 15x that lost), momentum 0.95 still averages ~20 steps (~1,900 records). Counter-risks: extra gradient noise at the 0.1 LR floor makes the handoff checkpoint noisier, the 067-style seed collapse recurs, and the gain from 066 was already at its optimum. RL, eval, and sampling speed are untouched (same architecture), so no timeout risk beyond the incumbent's.
expected_delta: -30 to +20 theorems at >=7 vs 081's 403.67 (central -5, since 081's 3-seed mean likely includes luck: nine follow-ups since scored 324-371); pretrain steps ~5,300-5,700 (081: 4,682/4,732/4,769); epochs ~3.2-3.5 (081: 3.89); final val loss 0.090-0.100 (081: 0.0950/0.0912/0.0964); held-out greedy 0.983-0.992; totals within ~+-60 s of 081

arch.change: none versus 081-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 081-claude; only the batch size changes)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

batch.note: CHANGED: 128 -> 96 records per optimizer step (only edit: the BS knob). val_loss chunks the 1024 val records in 96s, same value. records_seen = steps * 96.

config.init: Same as 081-claude: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights per seed identical to 081-claude; the data-order permutation and shift-augmentation generator is the same seeded stream but consumed in 96-record batches, so batch composition and shift draws differ from 081.
